rounds.proof_sketch: Per-element difference in else branch = 0.005*beta = 0.005. With 524,288 elements, max mean difference = 524288*0.005/524288 = 0.005. Tolerance threshold = atol + rtol*|ref| >= 0.01. Since 0.005 < 0.01, the mutation cannot be detected.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the constant from 0.5f to 0.495f in the L1 branch of smooth L1 loss. This produces a per-element difference of exactly 0.005 when abs_diff >= beta. Since the final output is the mean over all 524,288 elements, even if every single element hits the mutated branch, the maximum mean difference is 0.005. The torch.allclose tolerance with atol=0.01 requires a difference exceeding 0.01 + 0.01*|ref| to kill the mutant. Since 0.005 < 0.01, no input value pattern can produce a detectable difference under this tolerance.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the maximum achievable output difference (0.005) is mathematically bounded below the minimum tolerance threshold (0.01). Would require either: (1) reducing atol below 0.005, or (2) changing the beta parameter to increase the per-element difference.
rounds.recommendations: When setting mutation testing tolerances, ensure atol is smaller than the minimum perturbation delta that could be introduced by constant mutations. Here, a 1% perturbation of 0.5 produces a 0.005 difference in mean loss, which requires atol < 0.005 to detect. Consider using atol=1e-3 for tighter mutation detection.
